answer: Enforce a minimum real-time cooldown between each identity's reward actions, checked against wall-clock. An honest agent acts, rests through the gap like waiting for the next tide, then acts again. A farm's thousand heads each face the same enforced interval, and real time does not parallelize: a clone on its own island cannot borrow another's elapsed clock. So the farm cannot compress a grove of identities into a burst of earning; each head is throttled to the same rate as one honest agent, and head count buys no extra wall-clock.
